_comment: XFAIL registry: compatibility invariants that phantom does NOT currently satisfy.
These are open protocol bugs tracked in TODO.md, not harness defects.
A registered case that fails is reported as XFAIL and does not fail the build.
A registered case that PASSES fails the build with an XPASS error - that forces
whoever fixes the bug to delete its entry here in the same change. The registry
is therefore always an accurate, self-maintaining list of open protocol bugs.
To retire an entry: fix the bug, delete the entry, watch the test go green.

failures.reason: PongData is a fixed 12-field struct, so any field beyond Port6 is dropped on rebuild. Every real modern server sends 13.
failures.todo: TODO.md > Protocol correctness > 'Pong rewrite silently drops fields beyond the 12 known ones'

failures.reason: ReadUnconnectedPing discards the packet ID without checking it, so a 0x01 ping parses as a pong.
failures.todo: TODO.md > Bugs > 'Short/truncated packets parse silently into garbage'

failures.reason: The 16-byte RakNet magic is read but never compared against the expected constant.
failures.todo: TODO.md > Protocol correctness > 'No validation of magic bytes or packet length before parsing'

failures.reason: bytes.Buffer.Read partial-fills without returning an error, so a truncated pong yields a zero-padded struct instead of a parse failure.
failures.todo: TODO.md > Bugs > 'Short/truncated packets parse silently into garbage'

failures.reason: rewriteUnconnectedPong rewrites only the ServerID string field; the binary ServerGUID at bytes 9-16 passes through untouched.
failures.todo: TODO.md > Protocol correctness > 'Offline pong sends a zero binary ServerGUID; rewrite only touches the string ID'

failures.reason: The canned OfflinePong carries an all-zero ping time and the offline reply path never stamps the client's ping time into it.
failures.todo: TODO.md > Protocol correctness > 'Offline pong doesn't echo the client's ping time'

failures.reason: The canned OfflinePong advertises binary ServerGUID = 0, so every phantom whose upstream is down claims GUID 0.
failures.todo: TODO.md > Protocol correctness > 'Offline pong sends a zero binary ServerGUID'

failures.reason: The server-offline reply path matches only UnconnectedPingID (0x01), so a client that pings with 0x02 gets nothing while upstream is down.
failures.todo: TODO.md > Protocol correctness > '0x02 (Unconnected Ping Open Connections) not recognized'
